costGuide.title: Jaguar AJ126 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting an AJ126 typically takes 12-16 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for an AJ126 engine replacement is the condition of the supercharger assembly and cooling system. Units where the water pump and supercharger snout coupler have been preemptively replaced command a slight premium but carry significantly lower long-term risk. Because this is a supercharged V6, a full AJ126 rebuild is considerably more complex and expensive than naturally aspirated variants. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for a detailed breakdown of what influences your final quote.

failures.title: Jaguar AJ126 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Water Pump and Coolant Crossover Leaks
items.whatHappens: The plastic coolant crossover pipes and the water pump itself are prone to premature failure. This leads to rapid, sometimes invisible coolant loss, which can quickly escalate to severe engine overheating and cylinder head warping.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the water pump and upgrading to aluminium crossover pipes is a straightforward preventative repair. If overheating has occurred, a full AJ126 engine replacement is often the only viable solution.

items.title: Supercharger Snout Coupler Wear
items.whatHappens: The isolator coupler inside the supercharger snout degrades over time, causing a distinct rattling or whining noise from the front of the engine, particularly at idle or during throttle lift-off.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the coupler is a relatively inexpensive preventative repair. However, if disintegration has caused internal rotor scoring, a full supercharger rebuild or complete AJ126 engine replacement may be required.

items.title: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear
items.whatHappens: While more robust than the older 4.2L and 5.0L V8s, the AJ126 can still experience timing chain tensioner wear, leading to chain stretch and a cold-start rattle.
items.repairVsReplace: Updating to revised tensioners is a known preventative measure. If ignored and chain skip occurs, catastrophic valve-to-piston contact is highly likely, necessitating a full unit replacement.

failures.goodYearsLine: The AJ126 is generally considered more robust than its larger V8 siblings, but proactive cooling system maintenance remains the critical factor in its long-term longevity .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the AJ126
variants.intro: ═══════════════════════════════════════ The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible near the front timing cover, or listed on the VIN plate under the bonnet. The AJ126 is frequently confused with the larger Jaguar AJ133 5.0 V8 SC or the naturally aspirated Jaguar AJ-V6 3.0 NA. Fitting a 5.0L AJ133 into an AJ126 vehicle requires extensive ECU remapping, different engine mounts, and altered cooling architecture, making exact code matching critical to avoid costly installation errors.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement AJ126 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used AJ126 is only advisable for lower-value host vehicles and must come with verifiable proof that the water pump, coolant crossover pipes, and supercharger coupler have been replaced. Without this documented history, the risk of inheriting a failing cooling system or supercharger snout is unacceptably high. Explore our vetted used AJ126 engines for sale

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned AJ126 addresses the core weaknesses of this generation. It will include a new water pump, upgraded aluminium coolant crossover pipes, and a refreshed supercharger coupler. This is the most sensible, cost-effective route for preserving an XF, XJ, or F-Type without the unpredictability of a used unit. Compare reconditioned AJ126 options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples showing signs of bore wear, or if the engine has already suffered overheating damage. A quality rebuild should include line-boring, new pistons and rings, and a complete overhaul of the supercharged valvetrain to exceed factory specifications. Discuss a custom AJ126 rebuild

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our network of vetted UK Jaguar specialists can supply the unit and handle the complex installation, backing the work with a nationwide warranty so you have a single point of contact for the entire job. View supply and fit options
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For typical host vehicles like the 2013-2019 Jaguar XJ X351 or XF X260, current market values often sit between £8,000 and £25,000 . With reconditioned replacement costs starting around £4,500, the replacement is generally financially viable. However, for older or higher-mileage examples approaching the lower end of this band, if the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Jaguar AJ126 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned Jaguar AJ126 engine typically starts from £4,500 for supply-only, with fitted costs reflecting the complexity of the supercharged valvetrain. Supply-only reconditioned units generally range from £4,500 to £7,500. Independent fitting labour typically adds 12-16 hours at approximately £65/hr. Quotes sourced through our network include a minimum 12-month warranty.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the AJ126?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dominant failure patterns on the AJ126 are water pump failure, coolant crossover pipe leaks, and supercharger snout coupler wear. Plastic coolant components become brittle, leading to rapid coolant loss and potential overheating. A failing supercharger isolator coupler produces a distinct rattling or whining noise at idle or on throttle lift-off. Timing chain tensioner wear can also occur, though it is less catastrophic than on older Jaguar V8s.

mainEntity.name: Which Jaguar models use the AJ126 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The supercharged 3.0L AJ126 V6 was fitted to the Jaguar XF (X260), XJ (X351), and F-Type (X152) between 2013 and 2020. It served as the core performance petrol engine, balancing strong torque with better efficiency than the 5.0L V8. It is mechanically distinct from the naturally aspirated 3.0L V6 and the supercharged 5.0L V8. Always verify your specific chassis code before ordering a replacement unit.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a used or reconditioned AJ126 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: A reconditioned AJ126 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known age-related weaknesses of the cooling system and supercharger components. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting degraded coolant crossover pipes or a worn supercharger coupler. Proper reconditioning proactively upgrades these specific weak points with revised or metal components. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, unlike the 3-6 months typical for used engines.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my car has the AJ126 and not the 5.0L AJ133 or a naturally aspirated V6?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can confirm your engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet or the stamped code on the engine block near the front timing cover. The AJ126 is exclusively a 3.0L supercharged V6, visually identifiable by the Roots-type supercharger sitting in the valley of the engine. It is commonly confused with the larger 5.0L AJ133 or the older naturally aspirated 3.0L V6. Fitting the wrong revision will cause severe ECU mapping, supercharger plumbing, and engine mount compatibility issues.
